title: Adding Zika Virus to the FDA Priority Review Voucher Program Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on March 15, 2016. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Adding Zika Virus to the FDA Priority Review Voucher Program Act

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to add Zika virus disease to the list of tropical diseases under the priority review voucher program, which awards a voucher to the sponsor of a new drug or biological product that is approved to prevent or treat a tropical disease. (A voucher entitles the holder to have a future new drug or biological product application acted upon by the Food and Drug Administration within six months.)

The bill makes a technical correction to the tropical disease list to refer to filovirus disease, a condition caused by the family of viruses that includes the Ebola virus, instead of the family of viruses.

summary.headline: This law adds Zika virus to the list of tropical diseases that qualify for an FDA priority review voucher program.
summary.what_it_does: The law changes the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act so that Zika virus disease counts as a tropical disease under the priority review voucher program. Under that program, a company that gets approval for a new drug or biological product to prevent or treat a tropical disease receives a voucher. The voucher lets the holder have a future drug application reviewed by the Food and Drug Administration within six months. The law also fixes wording in the list so it refers to filovirus disease, the family of viruses that includes Ebola, instead of the broader family of viruses.

who_it_affects.group: Drug and biologics companies developing treatments for Zika virus
who_it_affects.how: They can earn a priority review voucher if their Zika prevention or treatment product is approved, which can speed review of a later application.

who_it_affects.group: People at risk of Zika virus infection
who_it_affects.how: The program may encourage development of Zika prevention or treatment products, though the law itself does not create any new drug.

who_it_affects.group: Companies developing treatments for filovirus diseases such as Ebola
who_it_affects.how: The corrected wording clarifies that the voucher program's tropical disease list refers to filovirus disease.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on April 19, 2016.
